thresholds._comment: EvalLens quality-gate thresholds. DETERMINISTIC thresholds were set from the measured baseline run evallens/runs/20261110T142928Z.json (67 questions, extractive/offline mode, commit b2ab7dd): faithfulness 1.000, answer_relevancy 0.613, context_precision 0.953, context_recall 0.997, refusal_accuracy 0.167. Each threshold sits ~0.05 below its baseline aggregate, so a real regression fails the gate while ordinary run-to-run noise passes. JUDGE thresholds are conservative initial values (0.60) — tighten them after the first measured Groq-judge run, because no judge-mode baseline exists yet (no GROQ_API_KEY was available when the harness was built). NOTE on refusal_accuracy (deterministic): 0.167 is a KNOWN WEAKNESS of the extractive fallback, not a target — without an LLM, Knowlix returns the most relevant passage for unanswerable questions instead of refusing (only the adversarial password question refused, because the sanitizer strips the injected sentence). The judge-mode threshold of 0.80 is the real target for production behaviour; the deterministic 0.15 only guards against getting worse than the known-bad baseline.

1. Upgrade sewage‑treatment facilities at Erode and Tiruchirappalli. [p. 6]  
2. Create riparian buffer zones of 30 metres along urban stretches of the river. [p. 6]  
3. Install real‑time water‑quality monitoring at six priority stations by June 2026. [p. 6]  
4. Launch a community‑reporting mobile app for river‑water issues. [p. 6]

_Support: 8/8 claims backed by the document._

results.question: Summarize the Kaveri water quality findings.
results.expected_answer: The Kaveri study monitored 18 stations from January to December 2025. pH stayed within the acceptable range, 14 of 18 stations met the dissolved oxygen standard, but biochemical oxygen demand exceeded its limit at 6 stations and total coliform peaked at 24,000 MPN per 100 millilitres at Tiruchirappalli. The study recommends sewage treatment upgrades, 30-metre buffer zones, real-time monitoring and a community app, at an estimated cost of 86 crore rupees over three years.
results.answer:
The 2025 Kaveri River Basin Water Quality Study monitored 18 stations from Talakaveri (Karnataka) to Poompuhar (Tamil Nadu) with monthly samples taken throughout the year [Page 1]. Six water‑quality parameters were analysed: pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), biochemical oxygen demand, total coliform, turbidity and nitrate [Page 1].

**pH**  
* The river’s pH across all stations varied between 6.8 and 8.4, which lies within the acceptable range of 6.5–8

_Support: 3/3 claims backed by the document._
